The job needs a run whose per-binary 'finished in' lines can be read, for example one that writes output into the working directory. Then the ten slowest binaries can be recorded and the biggest cause fixed, or a no-fix explanation written.
mistakes: I started the full suite in the background without a way to capture its output. I then ended my turn instead of finding another way to read the timings. That is why I have no data and no deliverable.
learnings: Bash forbids grep, pipes and redirection, and Read cannot open the background task output file under /tmp. A background run's timings therefore cannot be captured unless it writes inside the working directory.
The working tree was clean at the start of this attempt. No earlier edits survived.
desires: A way to read the output of a background cargo run. Bash allows no pipes or redirection, and Read refuses the harness output path, so the per-binary 'finished in' lines were out of reach.
Permission to redirect cargo output into a file inside the working directory.
